rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wisdom permits a small evil when it prevents a much greater evil, as removing a diseased limb can save the whole body.
rows.anchor: بيان أن الحكمة تقتضي ما يغلب خيره فإن ترك الخير الكثير لأجل الشر القليل شر كثير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating the locative phrase emphasizes how implausible the angels find the prospect of corruption on earth.
rows.anchor: وفائدة تكرار الظرف تأكيد الاستبعاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels mean unjustly spilling blood, and the wording names bloodshed because it is the ugliest kind of killing.
rows.anchor: أي : يصبها ظلما كما يسفك بنو الجان والتعبير عن القتل بسفك الدماء لما أنه أقبح أنواع القتل

rows.speaker: بعض العارفين
rows.claim: Some gnostics identify the disputers as earth angels, jinn, and devils dominated by darkness, rather than heavenly angels who recognize the Perfect Human’s rank.
rows.anchor: قال بعض العارفين الملائكة الذين نازعوا في آدم ليسوا من أهل الجبروت ولا من أهل الملكوت السماوية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning earth signals that earth angels challenged Adam; heavenly angels administer the upper world, while earth angels envied the caliphate and their own dominion.
rows.anchor: بتخصيص الأرض بالذكر وإن كان خليفة في العالم كله في الحقيقة هو إيماء أيضا بأن ملائكة الأرض هم الطاعنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels’ objection and dispute before the wise Creator is excused because of His perfect wisdom and workmanship.
rows.anchor: وأما الاعتراض على فعل الحكيم والنزاع في صنعه عند حضرته فمعفو عنه لكمال حكمته وإتقان صنعته

rows.speaker: المثنوي
rows.claim: The Mathnawi says divine mercy precedes wrath and that God’s disclosure of this precedence places the impulse to question in the listener.
rows.anchor: قال في "المثنوي" : زانكه أين دمها اكر نالا يقست رحمت من بر غضب هم سابقست

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The continuation of the Mathnawi image compares the angels’ forbearance to foam on a sea of divine forbearance: foam passes, while the sea remains.
rows.anchor: حلم ايشان كف بحر حلم ماست كف رود آيد ولى دريا بجاست

rows.speaker: الفتوحات
rows.claim: The Futuhat says Harut and Marut were among the angels who disputed Adam and were tested by God through manifesting corruption and bloodshed.
rows.anchor: وفي "الفتوحات" أن هاروت وماروت من الملائكة الدين نازعوا آدم ولأجل هذا ابتلاهما الله تعالى بإظهار الفساد وسفك الدماء

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet warns against gloating over a brother’s misfortune, since God may relieve him and test the one who gloats.
rows.anchor: فافهم سر قوله عليه السلام : "دع الشماتة عن أخيك فيعافيه الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some angels sent to aid the fighters also shed blood, but do so zealously in defense of God’s religion and law.
rows.anchor: وأيضا من تلك الملائكة الطاعنين بسفك الدماء الملائكة التي أرسلها الله تعالى نصرة للمجاهدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tasbih declares God free of what is unfitting; praise recalls His blessings; taqdis describes Him with fitting exaltation and denies what is unfitting.
rows.anchor: فالتسبيح لإظهار صفات الجلال والحمد لتذكير صفات الأنعام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām in “for You” may explain the act, as in a supplication formula, or be an added particle; the implied object is sanctifying God.
rows.anchor: فاللام للبيان كما في سقيا لك متعلقة بمصدر محذوف ويجوز أن تكون مزيدة

rows.speaker: التيسير
rows.claim: Al-Taysir distinguishes tasbih as negating what is unfitting for God and taqdis as affirming what is fitting for Him.
rows.anchor: قال في "التيسير" التسبيح نفي ما لا يليق به والتقديس إثبات ما يليق به

rows.speaker: داود القيصري
rows.claim: Dawud al-Qaysari says tasbih is broader: taqdis also negates perfections ascribed to created things, since their attachment to creation restricts them.
rows.anchor: وقال الشيخ داود القيصري قدس سره التسبيح أعم من التقديس لأنه تنزيه الحق عن نقائص الإمكان والحدوث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels’ question expresses their claim to greater entitlement to the caliphate and asks why humans were preferred despite their expected corruption.
rows.anchor: والمقصود عرض أحقيتهم منهم بالخلافة والاستفسار عما رجح بني آدم عليهم مع ما هو متوقع منهم من الفساد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows the wisdom of appointing Adam: his descendants include obedient and disobedient people, through whom merit and justice become manifest; creatures cannot know the Creator’s hidden governance.
rows.anchor: من الحكمة والمصلحة باستخلاف آدم عليه السلام وإن من ذريته الطائع والعاصي فيظهر الفضل والعدل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The seeker should show humility before God, His caliphs, shaykhs, and scholars, avoiding ego and displays of knowledge; one pursuing annihilation should not admire the self.
rows.anchor: وفي الآية تنبيه للسالك بأن يتأدب بين يدي الحق تعالى وخلفائه والمشايخ والعلماء لئلا يظهر بالأنانية

rows.speaker: السعدي
rows.claim: Saʿdi’s poem warns against approaching a temptation after seeing another caught by it, and against learning from others’ misfortunes only when they befall oneself.
rows.anchor: قال السعدي : نرود مرغ سوى دانه فراز ون دكر مرغ بيند اندربند

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The Najmiyya interpretation says jaʿl is broader than creation: it includes creating Adam and additionally endowing him with the special attribute of caliphate, as with David.
rows.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : {وإذ قال ربك للملائكة إني جاعل فى الارض خليفة} إنما قال جاعل وما قال خالق لمعنيين

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: It also assigns jaʿl to the world of Command and malakut, in contrast with creation of the sensory world; the Qur’an calls heavens and earth created but darkness and light made.
rows.anchor: أن للجعلية اختصاصا بعالم الأمور وهو للملكوت وهو ضد عالم الخلق لأنه هو عالم الأجسام والمحسوسات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This reading treats darkness and light as malakuti rather than sensory realities, since sensory darkness and light are already contained in the heavens and earth.
rows.anchor: وإنما قلنا الظلمات والنور من الملكوتيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adam is called created from clay in reference to his body, but made a caliph in reference to his spirit; this marks his distinction and dignity.
rows.anchor: فكذلك لما أخبر الله تعالى عن آدم بما يتعلق بجسمانيته ذكره بالخلقية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s announcement of Adam’s caliphate displays his honor to the angels, so they should revere him rather than reject the human traits shown by him and his descendants.
rows.anchor: وفي إني جاعل إشارة أخرى وهو إظهار عزة آدم عليه السلام على الملائكة لينظروا إليه بنظر التعظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One purpose of calling Adam caliph is to show that God graciously accepted humanity for servanthood and caliphate, encouraging people not to despair but to continue serving.
rows.anchor: ومنها لنعلم أن الله تعالى من كمال فضله وكرمه قد قبلنا بالعبودية والخلافة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Caliphate depends on spiritual preparedness and capacity, which angels lack; the seeker must value and work to attain this great capacity.
rows.anchor: ومنها لنعلم أن فساد الاستعداد أمر عظيم وبناء جسيم ومبنى الخلافة على الاستعداد والقابلية وليس للملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Angels saw Adam’s body before the spirit was breathed into it and perceived its elemental mixture and human, animal, and predatory traits, reasoning by analogy with animals already created.
rows.anchor: لأنهم نظروا إلى جسد آدم قبل نفخ الروح فشاهدوا بالنظر الملكي في ملكوت جسده المخلوق من العناصر الأربعة المتضادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What is unseen depends on the observer: the malakut is hidden from sensory humans but visible to angels and to people granted spiritual sight.
rows.anchor: وهذا لا يكون غيبا في حقهم وإنما يكون غيبا لنا لأنا ننظر بالحس والملكوت يكون لأهل الحس غيبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The malakut is witnessed by angels, while the divine presence remains hidden from them; they cannot ascend to that presence.
rows.anchor: فالغيب ما غاب عنك وما شاهدته فهو شهادة فالملكوت للملائكة شهادة والحضرة الإلهية لهم غيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humans unite a sensory body, a spirit from the unseen malakut, and a secret prepared to receive divine illumination; spiritual training raises them from the witnessed world to malakut.
rows.anchor: وإن في الإنسان صورة من عالم الشهادة المحسوسة وروحا من عالم الغيب الملكوتي غير المحسوس وسرا مستعدا لقبول فيض الأنوار الإلهية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Through following the Prophet, the human secret rises from malakut to jabarut and the hidden of the hidden, witnessing the lights of divine beauty and majesty and becoming a caliph of the seen and unseen.
rows.anchor: وبسر المتابعة وخصوصيتها يترقى من عالم الملكوت إلى عالم الجبروت والعظموت وهو غيب الغيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The human capacity for the hidden of the hidden is the concealed secret in human preparedness that God knows and the angels do not.
rows.anchor: فهذا هو السر المكنون المركوز في استعداد الإنسان الذي كان الله يعلم منه والملائكة لا يعلمونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Persian poem urges one whose life has passed and whose root is dry to water it with repentance and the water of life, so life’s tree may endure.
rows.anchor: عمرا كربكذشت بيخش أين دم است آب توبش ده اكر اوبي نم است

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse recalls the seventy Israelite elders Moses chose to accompany him to the mountain to apologize for worship of the calf; they were not the first group of seventy chosen after Pharaoh drowned.
rows.anchor: السبعين من أسلافكم الذين اختارهم موسى حين ذهبوا معه إلى الطور للاعتذار عن عبادة العجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They refused to accept Moses’ claim that the book was from God, that he had heard God speak, and that God commanded them to accept and follow it until they saw God.
rows.anchor: لن نصدقك لأجل قولك ودعوتك على أن هذا كتاب الله وأنك سمعت كلامه وأن الله تعالى أمرنا بقبوله والعمل به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jahra means seeing God openly, face to face, without a barrier, with the clarity associated with an audible utterance.
rows.anchor: لا ساتر بيننا وبينه كالجهر في الوضوح والانكشاف لأن الجهر في المسموعات والمعاينة في المبصرات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jahra is accusative as a verbal noun describing a kind of seeing, or as a circumstantial accusative modifying either the seers or God as the seen.
rows.anchor: ونصبها عن المصدرية لأنها نوع من الرؤية فكأنها مصدر الفعل الناصب أو حال من الفاعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The saʿiqa is a burning fire with a sound descending from the sky, or any terrifying event that kills or removes reason; it can be sound, fire, or another form.
rows.anchor: هي نار محرقة فيها صوت نازلة من السماء وهي كل أمر مهول مميت أو مزيل للعقل والفهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They were struck for stubbornly demanding an impossible earthly vision of God; vision without modality is possible for believers in the afterlife and for select prophets in some worldly states.
rows.anchor: وإنما أحرقتهم الصاعقة لسؤالهم ما هو مستحيل على الله في الدنيا ولفرط العناد والتعنت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They saw the descending lightning or fire; if it was a terrifying sound, some died first and the others saw that they had died, figuratively called seeing death.
rows.anchor: فقد مات بعضهم أولا ورأى السابقون أنهم ماتوا ويسمى هذا رؤية الموت مجازا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is not unaware of their wrongs and will repay them at resurrection; this is a severe warning against sin and glad tidings for the obedient, since rights will reach their rightful owners.
rows.anchor: لا يخفى عليه شيء من أعمالهم فيجازيهم بها يوم البعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those described chose worldly life and turned away from the afterlife, although they could have gained it; they rejected parts of scripture to preserve benefits from their allies.
rows.anchor: الموصوفون بما ذكر من الأوصاف القبيحة

words: فَلَا يُخَفَّفُ عَنْهُمُ ٱلْعَذَابُ وَلَا هُمْ يُنصَرُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their punishment will not be lightened, whether worldly or otherworldly, and no one can rescue them by warding it off through intercession or force.
rows.anchor: دنيويا كان أو أخرويا {ولا هم ينصرون} يمنعون من العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author likens their choice to a bad trade: one cannot attain the pleasures of both worlds, and pursuing one forfeits the other; a person who trades the afterlife for worldly pleasures is especially blameworthy.
rows.anchor: فإذا اشتغل بتحصيل إحداهما فقد فوت الأخرى على نفسه فجعل الله ما أعرض اليهود عنه من الإيمان بما في كتابهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wise should seek the afterlife, resist Satan’s commands for egoistic gain, and remain in the religion of primordial nature rather than stray into misery.
rows.anchor: فعلى العاقل أن يرغب في تجارة الآخرة ولا يركن إلى الدنيا ولا يسفك دمه بامتثال أوامر الشيطان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition on shedding one’s blood also forbids exhausting oneself through severe hardship, wandering in the desert, or avoiding homes in religious ignorance and folly.
rows.anchor: إشارة أخرى إلى أن العبد ولا يجوز له أن يقتل نفسه من جهد أو بلاء يصيبه أو يهيم في الصحراء

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Some Companions planned extreme asceticism; the Prophet said he prays and sleeps, fasts and breaks fast, has relations, lives in homes, and eats meat, and that whoever rejects his sunna is not of him; they relented.
rows.anchor: فقال عليه السلام : "إني أصلي وأنام وأصوم وأفطر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author quotes the directive to give every person their due right as the principle behind balanced religious practice.
rows.anchor: قال تعالى : "وآت كل ذي حق حقه" فالكمال في التجاوز عن القيود والوصول إلى عالم الشهود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gnostic sees only God in all mirrors and manifestations and thus has nowhere to flee, since wherever one turns, God’s face is there.
rows.anchor: وعين العارف لا ترى غير الله في المرايا والمظاهر

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An aphorism says a sincere knowledge seeker, fulfilling his obligations in devotion, would keep studying even if told he will die tomorrow and would wish to meet death in that state.
rows.anchor: ولذا قيل : الذي يطلب العلمإذا قيل له غدا تموت لا يضيع الكتاب من يده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tawba means return; God’s tawba is accepting a servant’s repentance, creating return in the sinner’s heart, and replacing outward sins with obedience. Tawwab intensifies the abundance of this acceptance.
rows.anchor: أصل التوبة الرجوع وتوبة الله على العبد قبوله توبته وأن يخلق الانابة والرجوع في قلب المسيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prayer asks for a messenger from among the Muslim community descended from Abraham and Ishmael; being sent among them does not itself entail being one of them.
rows.anchor: أي : من أنفسهم فإن البعث فيهم لا يستلزم البعث منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad is the only prophet from Abraham and Ishmael’s descendants, and he is the one who answers their prayer.
rows.anchor: ولم يبعث من ذريتهما غير النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فهو الذي أجيب به دعوتهما

rows.speaker: راوٍ غير مسمى
rows.claim: A report says Abraham was told his prayer would be answered at the end of time.
rows.anchor: روي أنه قيل له قد استجيب لك وهو في آخر الزمان

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet says he was designated the Seal of Prophets while Adam was still in clay, and names Abraham’s prayer, Jesus’ good news, and his mother’s vision of light illuminating Syrian palaces as the beginnings of his mission.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث "إني عند الله مكتوب خاتم النبيين وأن آدم لمجدل في طينته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham’s specific invocation was the request that God send a messenger among the Israelites.
rows.anchor: وأراد بدعوة إبراهيم هذا فإنه دعا الله أن يبعث في بني إسرائيل رسولا منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The messenger recites and conveys revelations that establish monotheism and prophethood.
rows.anchor: يقرأ عليهم ويبلغهم ما يوحى إليه من دلائل التوحيد والنبوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Teaching develops their theoretical faculty: the Book is the Qur’an, and wisdom is true knowledge and the religious rulings that perfect the soul.
rows.anchor: وما يكمل به نفوسهم من المعارف الحقة والأحكام الشرعية

rows.speaker: ابن دريد
rows.claim: Ibn Durayd defines wisdom as any saying that admonishes, directs someone toward virtue, or forbids a wrong.
rows.anchor: قال ابن دريد : كل كلمة وعظتك أو دعتك إلى مكرمة أو نهتك عن قبيح فهي حكمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Purification develops the practical faculty by cleansing people of polytheism and sins, whether through neglecting duties or committing wrongs.
rows.anchor: من دنس الشرك وفنون المعاصي سواء كانت بترك الواجبات أو بفعل المنكرات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham closes with praise: God is mighty, prevailing over what He wills, and wise, acting only as wisdom and benefit require; all else is inherently weak and ignorant.
rows.anchor: الذي يقهر ويغلب على ما يريد

rows.speaker: الإمام الغزالي
rows.claim: Al-Ghazali begins defining the Divine Name al-ʿAziz as one who is eminent and rare, urgently needed, and difficult to reach.
rows.anchor: قال الإمام الغزالي قدس سره في "شرح الأسماء الحسنى" العزيز : هو الخطير الذي يقل وجود مثله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sending messengers serves a wise benefit: they order outward life, illuminate the inward, and organize the world; their heirs, the perfected saints, inherit a special share in purification.
rows.anchor: لأن عمارة الظاهر وإنارة الباطن ونظام العالم بهم لا بغيرهم ولورثتهم من الأولياء الكاملين حظ أوفى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A servant needs a guide and spiritual mentor to reach the goal; without a shaykh, Satan becomes his shaykh.
rows.anchor: فلا بد للعبد من دليل ومرشد يهتدي به إلى مقصوده ومن لم يكن له شيخ فشيخه الشيطان

rows.speaker: الحافظ
rows.claim: Hafiz’s Persian verse cautions against entering the path of love without a guide, since self-directed striving failed him despite great effort.
rows.anchor: قال الحافظ : بكوى عشق منه بي دليل رآه قدم كه من بخويش نمودم صد اهتمام ونشد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A perfected guide, with God’s permission, purifies the seeker from attention to anything besides God and recites signs within the self and in the horizons, leading to certainty, spiritual joy, and the company of the truthful.
rows.anchor: والمرشد الكامل يزكي نفس السالك بإذن الله ويطهرها من دنس الالتفات إلى ما سوى الله ويتلو عليه الآيات الأنفسية والآفاقية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase “and purifies them” points to spiritual wayfaring and guiding; the passage ends with a prayer for protection from obstacles on the path to God.
rows.anchor: يشير إلى السلوك والتسليك فاحفظ هذا وليكن على ذكر منك اللهم احفظنا من الموانع في طريق الوصول إليك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Persian lines value freedom and death as a passage to greater life; the wise should subdue the self through spiritual discipline and enliven the heart with abiding life.
rows.anchor: شير مولى جويد آزادىء ومرك ونكه اندر مرك بيند صد وجود همو روانه بسوزاند وجود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The arrival of death means its causes and signs have appeared, such as illnesses and symptoms, rather than the instant of death itself.
rows.anchor: حضر أسبابه وظهر أمارته وآثاره من العلل والأمراض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person cannot make a bequest at the actual moment of death, which is why the verse refers to the onset and signs of death.
rows.anchor: إذ لا اقتدار على الوصية عند حضور نفس الموت والعامل في إذا مدلول كتب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The semantic content of “was prescribed” governs the conditional; the prescription does not first occur at death, but its application to the person begins then.
rows.anchor: والعامل في إذا مدلول كتب لأن الكتب بمعنى الإيجاب لا يحدث وقت حضور الموت بل الحادث تعلقه بالمكلف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording “was prescribed” signals that this obligation was inscribed in pre-eternity, though it applies to the person at the onset of death.
rows.anchor: فكأنه قيل توجه عليكم إيجاب الله تعالى ومقتضى كتابه إذا حضر فعبر عن توجه الإيجاب وتعلقه بكتب للدلالة على أن هذا المعنى مكتوب في الأزل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khayr here means property, whether little or much, though ordinary Arabic does not call someone a possessor of wealth when their property is small.
rows.anchor: {إن ترك خيرا} أي : مالا قليلا أو كثيرا

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha advised a man with three thousand and four dependents to leave his modest wealth to his children rather than make a bequest.
rows.anchor: وعن عائشة رضي الله عنها "أن رجلا أراد أن يوصي قالت : كم مالك؟ قال : ثلاثة آلاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The basic sense of good is anything desirable and beneficial, the opposite of evil.
rows.anchor: وأصل الخير أن يكون لكل ما يرغب فيه مما هو نافع لأنه ضد الشر

rows.speaker: إخوان الصفا
rows.claim: The Brethren of Purity define good as doing what ought to be done, at the right time, for the right reason.
rows.anchor: قال في "إخوان الصفا" الخير فعل ما ينبغي في الوقت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-wasiyya is the passive subject of “was prescribed,” meaning that making a bequest was enjoined.
rows.anchor: نائب فاعل كتب أي : فرض الإيصاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The recipients are parents and close relatives, whether or not they inherit.
rows.anchor: ممن يرث ومن لا يرث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fair bequest should not exceed a third, favor the rich while leaving the poor, or violate justice.
rows.anchor: بالعدل لا يزيد على الثلث ولا يوصي لغني ويدع الفقير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In pre-Islamic custom, people bequeathed to distant outsiders for show and prestige while leaving close relatives poor; early Islam redirected those bequests to parents and relatives.
rows.anchor: وكان السبب في نزول هذه الآية أن أهل الجاهلية كانوا يوصون بمالهم للبعدى رياء وسمعة طلبا للفخر والشرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bequest ruling applied when it served justice and wisdom, then was abrogated by the inheritance verse in Surat al-Nisa; bequests are no longer obligatory and may go to non-heirs, but not heirs.
rows.anchor: فعمل بها ما كان العمل بها صلاحا وحكمة ثم نسختها آية المواريث في سورة النساء فالآن لا يجب على أحد أن يوصي لأحد قريب ولا بعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The obligation protects wealth from waste and relatives from deprivation; those who truly fear God should not abandon this practice as originally prescribed.
rows.anchor: أي : أحق هذه الوصية حقا

rows.speaker: ابن الشيخ
rows.claim: Ibn al-Shaykh answers that the phrase does not restrict the duty to already pious people; it means the duty binds everyone who chooses and pursues piety.
rows.anchor: قال ابن الشيخ في "حواشيه" : فإن قيل قوله : على المتقين يقتضي

rows.speaker: جعفر الصادق
rows.claim: Jaʿfar al-Sadiq says the sweetness of being addressed removes the hardship of worship: a lover hastens to obey the beloved, even if commanded to enter the fire.
rows.anchor: وقال جعفر الصادق لذة في النداء أزال بها تعب العبادة والعناء يشير إلى أن المحب يبادر إلى امتثال أمر محبوبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prescribed fast is the fast of Ramadan, as clarified by the following references to counted days and to witnessing the month.
rows.anchor: فرض عليكم صيام شهر رمضان فإنه تعالى قال بعده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In legal usage, fasting is daytime abstention with intention by an eligible person from the familiar invalidators, which comprise the main things the self desires.
rows.anchor: والصيام في الشريعة هو الإمساك نهارا مع النية من أهله عن المفطرات المعهودة التي هي معظم ما تشتهيه الأنفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ordinary believer fasts by abstaining from invalidators, while the spiritual elite also abstain from prohibited acts.
rows.anchor: وهذا صوم عوام المؤمنين وأما صوم الخواص فالإمساك عن المنهيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The highest spiritual elite fast by abstaining from everything besides God.
rows.anchor: وأما صوم أخص الخواص فالامساك عما سوى الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kama kutiba can be parsed as an adjective modifying an omitted verbal noun, or as a circumstantial phrase with ma as a relative pronoun.
rows.anchor: محل كما النصب على أنه صفة مصدر محذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fasting was prescribed for prophets and communities from Adam onward; the comparison confirms the ruling and reassures people because a shared hardship is easier to bear.
rows.anchor: من الأنبياء عليهم السلام والأمم من لدن آدم عليه السلام وفيه تأكيد للحكم وترغيب فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison concerns the basic obligation, not the exact quantity or timing: Adam fasted the white days, and Moses’ people fasted on Ashura; likeness does not mean sameness in every respect.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن التشبيه عائد إلى أصل إيجاب الصوم لا إلى كمية الصوم المكتوب وبيان وقته فكان الصوم على آدم أيام البيض وصوم عاشوراء كان على قوم موسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fasting helps avoid sins by curbing desire, which is their source.
rows.anchor: المعاصي فإن الصوم يكسر الشهوة التي هي مبدؤها

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet advises young men who can marry to do so to lower the gaze and guard chastity; those unable should fast, which restrains sexual desire.
rows.anchor: يا معشر الشباب من استطاع منكم الباءة فليتزوج فإنه أغض للبصر وأحصن للفرج ومن لم يستطع فعليه بالصوم

rows.speaker: النووي
rows.claim: Al-Nawawi is cited for defining a young man, among the author’s school, as someone who has reached puberty but is not yet thirty.
rows.anchor: الشباب جمع شاب وهو عند أصحابنا من بلغ ولم يجاوز ثلاثين كذا قاله النووي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The days are specified and counted, or few in number; little wealth is counted piece by piece, while great wealth is poured out without measuring.
rows.anchor: موقتات ومقدرات بعدد معلوم أو قلائل فإن القليل من المال يعد عدا والكثير يهال هيلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God did not prescribe fasting all the time or most of the year, making the duty easier for all communities through mercy and relief.
rows.anchor: فالله تعالى لم يفرض علينا صيام الدهر ولا صيام أكثره تخفيفا ورحمة وتسهيلا لأمر التكليف على جميع الأمم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ayāman is accusative under an implied command to fast, either adverbially or as an extended direct object.
rows.anchor: وانتصاب أياما بمضمر دل هو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sick person is one harmed or further harmed by fasting; the travel concession applies to a person established on a journey, rather than someone who merely starts traveling during the day.
rows.anchor: يضره الصوم أو يضر معه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition ʿalā depicts the traveler as riding and controlling a mount; this is why the verse says “on a journey” instead of simply “traveling.”
rows.anchor: وكلمة على فيها استعارة تبعية شبه تلبسه بالسفر باستعلاء الراكب واستيلائه على المركوب يتصرف فيه كيف يشاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who break the fast due to illness or travel must make up the same number of days later, continuously or with intervals.
rows.anchor: فعليه صوم عدة أيام المرض والسفر فعدة من العد بمعنى المعدود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word ʿidda derives from counting and can also denote a counted group of people.
rows.anchor: فعدة من العد بمعنى المعدود ومنه يقال للجماعة المعدودة من الناس عدة

rows.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
rows.claim: Most exegetes say healthy residents initially could either fast or break the fast and feed a poor person; the choice was later abrogated by the command to fast when witnessing Ramadan.
rows.anchor: ذهب أكثر المفسرين إلى أن المراد بالذين يطيقونه الأصحاء المقيمون خيرهم في ابتداء الإسلام بين أمرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For those capable of fasting who used the former option to break it, the fidya was half a ṣāʿ of wheat or one ṣāʿ of another staple.
rows.anchor: وهي نصف صاع من بر أو صاع من غيره والفدية في معنى الجزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fidya is a form of recompense, a substitute given in place of the original act.
rows.anchor: والفدية في معنى الجزاء وهو عبارة عن البدل القائم عن الشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shahr Ramadan is a subject whose predicate follows; the sentence highlights the month’s virtue and explains why its fast was prescribed.
rows.anchor: مبتدأ خبره ما بعده فيكون المقصود من ذكر هذه الجملة المنبهة على فضله ومنزلته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fast of Ramadan is obligatory for whoever witnesses the month, as stated in the verse’s following command.
rows.anchor: ثم أوجب صومه بقوله : {فمن شهد منكم الشهر}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Arabic word for month is shahr because the month is widely known; Ramadan is a verbal noun from ramida, to burn, and the compound is a proper name made diptote by its ending.
rows.anchor: ورمضان مصدر رمض إذا احترق فأضيف إليه الشهر وجعل المجموع علما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ramadan may be named for livers burning from hunger and thirst, sins burning away through fasting, or the month’s occurrence during intense heat.
rows.anchor: وإنما سمي بذلك إما لارتماض الأكباد واحتراقها من الجوع والعطش وإما لارتماض الذنوب بالصيام فيه أو لوقوعه أيام رمض الحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One account says month names were borrowed from an older language and assigned according to the season at naming, as with Ramadan’s hot days, spring, and frozen water in Jumada.
rows.anchor: قيل : إنهم نقلوا أسماء الشهور من اللغة القديمة فسموها بالأزمنة التي وقعت هي فيها وقت التسمية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative view holds that Ramadan is one of God’s names; a Prophetic report therefore advises saying “the month of Ramadan,” not “Ramadan came” or “Ramadan went.”
rows.anchor: أو رمضان اسم من أسماء الله تعالى والشهر مضاف إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an first descended to Bayt al-ʿIzza in the lowest heaven, then Gabriel brought it down in portions over twenty-three years according to divine will.
rows.anchor: جملة إلى بيت العزة في السماء الدنيا ثم نزل به جبريل نجوما في ثلاث وعشرين سنة حسبما تقتضيه المشيئة الربانية

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A Prophetic report dates the Scrolls of Abraham to Ramadan’s first night, the Torah to its sixth day, the Gospel to its thirteenth, and the Qur’an to its twenty-fourth.
rows.anchor: وعن النبي عليه السلام : "نزلت صحف إبراهيم أول ليلة من رمضان وأنزلت التوراة لست مضين منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qur’an derives from qarʾ, gathering, because it brings together the knowledge of earlier and later people.
rows.anchor: والقرآن من القرء وهو الجمع لأنه مجمع علم الأولين والآخرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an was sent as guidance for people to the straight path, through its inimitability and other features.
rows.anchor: أي : أنزل حال كونه هداية للناس إلى سواء الصراط بما فيه من الإعجاز وغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an also contains clear signs guiding to truth and distinguishing it from falsehood through its wisdom and rulings; guidance has more than one category.
rows.anchor: أي : وحال كونه آيات واضحات مما يهدي إلى الحق
